corrected_content.problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the point $C(1,4,-14)$ and is parallel to the plane determined by the two distinct parallel lines $\mathbf{r}=⟨-1,5,7⟩+s⟨1,1,1⟩$ and $\mathbf{r}=⟨0,3,-19⟩+t⟨-2,-2,-2⟩.$
corrected_content.worked_solution:
The two lines have direction vectors $\mathbf d_1=\langle1,1,1\rangle$ and $\mathbf d_2=\langle-2,-2,-2\rangle=-2\mathbf d_1$, so they are parallel. Their base points are $P(-1,5,7)$ and $Q(0,3,-19)$. The vector between them is

$$
\mathbf u=\overrightarrow{PQ}=\langle1,-2,-26\rangle.
$$

The plane determined by the two lines has direction span $\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf d_1,\mathbf u\}$. These vectors are independent because $\mathbf d_1\times\mathbf u=\langle-24,27,-3\rangle\ne\mathbf0$. A parallel plane through $C(1,4,-14)$ has the same direction span, hence its parametric equation is

$$
\mathbf r=\langle1,4,-14\rangle+s\langle1,1,1\rangle+t\langle1,-2,-26\rangle,\qquad s,t\in\mathbb R.
$$

This is the unique listed plane with that direction span passing through $C$.
